TRAFFIC ADVISORY 

IN CONNECTION WITH PROTEST BEING HELD AT CHANDGI RAM AKHARA, MGM (RING ROAD) ON 04.08.25 

A Protest is being held on 04.08.2025 from 1130 hours at Chandgiram Akhara MGM (Ring Road).Due to the protest, traffic will remain affected on MGM (Ring Road) on 04.08.2025 from 11:30 AM onwards for general road users except emergency vehicles.

DIVERSION POINTS: -
1.     I.P College Red Light
2.Chandgiram Akhara.

All vehicles will be diverted from the above points as and when required.

ALTERNATE ROUTE:-
Traffic coming from ISBT Kashmiri Gate and Majnu Ka Tila on Chandigram Akhara :-

The traffic destined to I.P College and P. S Civil Lines from Outer Ring Road (ISBT Kashmiri gate) will be diverted from Chandgiram Akhara to Outer Ring Road -Baba Gopal Sahib Talab Road- Khyber Pass Red light and then take Mall road to reach their destinations.

The traffic destined to I.P College and P.S Civil Lines from Ouetr Ring Road (Majnu Ka Tila) will be diverted from Chandgiram Akhara to Outer Ring Road towards ISBT Kashmiri Gate.

Traffic coming from Khyber Pass and Shamnath Marg on Chandgiram Akhara:-

The traffic destined to ISBT from Khyber Pass will be diverted from I.P College Red Light to Shamnath Marg and then take Boulevard Road to reach their destinations.
The traffic destined to ISBT from Shamnath Marg will be diverted from I.P College Red Light to MGM P.S Civil Lines Red Light –Khyber Pass- Baba Gopal Sahib Talab Road and then take Outer Ring Road to reach their destinations.

INSTRUCTIONS TO GENERAL PUBLIC: -
1.    Commuters are advised to avoid the above roads.
2.Avoid roadside parking as it causes hindrance to    normal flow of traffic.

Behind Dubai’s glittering skyline, luxury malls, and futuristic towers lies a darker, hidden city—one built not by visionaries, but by invisible labor. The world sees Burj Khalifa, artificial islands, and opulence, but rarely sees the workers who made it all possible. These are the men and women shipped in from Bangladesh, India, Pakistan, Nepal, and the Philippines—promised jobs and a better life, only to find themselves trapped in a system that exploits their bodies and erases their dignity.

They are bused in at dawn from labor camps on the outskirts of the city—massive, prison-like compounds hidden from tourists and the elite. These workers often live eight or more to a room, with bunk beds stacked in sweltering, cramped quarters. Many have their passports confiscated upon arrival. They cannot leave without permission. They are not allowed to unionize or protest. In many cases, their wages are delayed or cut without explanation. This is not just exploitation—it is a system of indentured servitude dressed in the clothes of modern development.

The same applies to taxi drivers, nannies, construction workers, and cleaners. Taxi drivers work 12–16 hour shifts just to make enough to send a few dollars home. They sleep in communal apartments, sometimes hot-bedding in shifts. They're fined for minor infractions, and their income is tightly controlled. They are surveilled, squeezed, and forgotten. Yet without them, Dubai would cease to function. They are the gears turning beneath the golden facade.

The UAE’s Kafala system—where a worker’s legal status is tied to their employer—creates conditions ripe for abuse. It's legal serfdom, operating with a smile. Any attempt to resist or escape can result in detention, deportation, or worse. Meanwhile, the country markets itself as a global hub of innovation, culture, and prosperity—ignoring the very people who built the dream.

This isn't just a labor issue. It's a moral one. The global elite come to Dubai to escape taxes, flaunt wealth, and indulge in extravagance—oblivious or indifferent to the human toll. The architecture is stunning, but the foundation is stained. No amount of glass, steel, or imported luxury can hide the fact that this city was built on the backs of those who had no choice.

Dubai is not alone—many modern cities rely on hidden exploitation. But its contrast is stark: a hypermodern Disneyland for the rich resting on the daily exhaustion of a working class made invisible by design.

If justice means anything, it must include the hands that build our cities—not just the ones that profit from them.

data.raw_text:
ICYMI O/N & WEEKEND

TRADE:

USTR Greer said that tariffs Trump imposed last week on scores of countries are likely to stay in place rather than be cut as part of continuing negotiations. Greer also said recent trade talks with Beijing had been "very positive" and were focused on the supply of rare earth magnets and minerals. (CBS)

China is limiting the flow of critical minerals to Western defense manufacturers, delaying production and forcing companies to scour the world for stockpiles of the minerals needed to make everything from bullets to jet fighters. (WSJ)

Chinese exporters are reconsidering investment in offshore factories as US tariffs on alternative hubs and new restrictions on “transshipment” force a sweeping rethink of supply chains in Asia. (FT)

The Swiss government is open to revising its offer to the US in response to planned heavy tariffs, Business Minister Guy Parmelin said, as experts warned the 39% import duties announced by Trump could trigger a recession in Switzerland. (RTRS)

Japanese PM Ishiba said on Monday he will not hesitate to hold talks with US President Trump to ensure an agreed cut to U.S. automobile tariffs is implemented soon. (RTRS)

Trump and Canadian PM Carney will likely talk "over the next number of days" after the U.S. imposed a 35% tariff on goods not covered by the U.S.-Mexico-Canada trade agreement, a Canadian official said on Sunday. (RTRS)

South Korea’s presidential policy chief said the country’s $350 billion investment pledge as part of the US trade deal is largely structured as loan guarantees rather than direct capital injections, seeking to ease domestic concerns over the scale and risks of the agreement. (BBG)

The Philippines may temporarily suspend rice imports to support local farmers in the world’s biggest buyer, potentially increasing the risk of expanding a global surplus. (BBG)

MACRO:

Trump said on Friday that Fed Chair Powell will "most likely" stay in his position. Trump said he would remove Powell "in a heartbeat" and said the Fed's interest rate was too high but added that others have said Powell's removal would "disturb the market." (Newxmax)

Trump said he will announce a new head of BLS in the next three or four days. (RTRS)

White House Economic Advisor Hassett said that the firing of BLS commissioner Erika McEntarfer is part of Trump’s plan to make further changes to the agency. (NBC)

Trump said he is to announce replacement for Fed's Kugler in the next couple of days. (RTRS)

Fed's Williams said that he would go into the September policy meeting with "very much an open mind" about cutting interest rates. (WSJ)

OPEC+ agreed on Sunday to raise oil production by 547,000 barrels per day for September, the latest in a series of accelerated output hikes to regain market share, as concerns mount over potential supply disruptions linked to Russia. (RTRS)

Japanese PM Ishiba said on Monday the government is ready to compile an extra budget to cushion the economic blow from U.S. tariffs. Some analysts expect it could reach around 10 trillion yen ($67.68 billion), which would require additional debt issuance. (RTRS)

China will likely step up monetary easing efforts in the second half of this year by cutting benchmark interest rates and banks’ reserve requirements in order to guide overall financing costs lower and support the economy, according to analysts in China press. (Shanghai Securities News).

China said it plans to tax interest income on bonds issued by the government and financial institutions, in a surprise move that’s prompted investors to reevaluate their debt market positions. (BBG)

China’s local governments including Guangzhou are actively studying plans to tap the nation’s “new financing policy tool” to fund infrastructure investment. (China Securities Journal)

Copper rose for a second day as Chilean mining giant Codelco grappled with the aftermath of a deadly accident at one of the world’s biggest underground mines. (BBG)

South Korean stocks rose the most in Asia on Monday as opposition to a plan to hike tax on capital gains intensified. (BBG)

Iran and Iraq are close to resolving a dispute over disruptions to Iranian gas supplies and Baghdad’s unpaid dues for the exports, Iran’s Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad said Saturday. (BBG)

GEOPOLITICAL:

Trump said there will be sanctions if Russia does not stop the war, but that Russia seems to be good at avoiding sanctions, adding that special envoy Witkoff will be going to Russia on Wednesday or Thursday. (RTRS)

India will keep purchasing oil from Russia despite Trump's threats of penalties, two Indian government sources told Reuters on Saturday. (RTRS)

White House Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller on Sunday accused India of effectively financing Russia's war in Ukraine by purchasing oil from Moscow, after Trump escalated pressure on New Delhi to stop buying Russian oil. (RTRS)

'Home by Home, Russia Is Selling Occupied Ukraine to Russians' WSJ article notes Kremlin-linked construction firms reap profits from redevelopment of housing destroyed by Russia’s invasion. (WSJ)

EQUITIES:

Berkshire Hathaway said on Saturday it took a $3.76 billion write-down on its stake in Kraft Heinz during the second quarter, an acknowledgment the decade-old investment hasn't worked out. (WSJ)

Amphenol is nearing a deal to buy CommScope Holding’s broadband connectivity and cable unit, according to WJS sources. The deal would be valued at roughly $10.5 billion, including debt. (WSJ)

More than 3,200 union members who assemble Boeing's fighter jets in the St. Louis area and Illinois went on strike on Monday after rejecting a second contract offer the previous day. (RTRS)

US railroad customer groups have demanded regulators block or put onerous conditions on the proposed merger of Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern. (FT)

Meta has placed big orders to Taiwan's Quanta Computer for customized AI servers based on its next-generation ASIC (own chip, made with Broadcom). The order is seen at up to 6,000 cabinets, shipped by year-end. (UDN via @dnystedt)

Xiaomi on Monday released an open-source voice model to complement its automotive and home appliance technologies, further heating up the race to build AI tools for more than just text. (BBG)

China Mobile, the world's biggest wireless carrier by users, said on Monday it had bought a 14.4% stake in Hong Kong-based broadband service provider HKBN for HK$1.08 billion ($137.58 million). (RTRS)

UBS said it reached an agreement with the U.S. Justice Department to pay $300 million to resolve outstanding consumer-relief obligations Credit Suisse committed to. (WSJ)

DATA RECAP (Newsquawk)

Australian Melbourne Institute Inflation Gauge MM (Jul) 0.9% (Prev. 0.1%)
Australian Melbourne Institute Inflation Gauge YY (Jul) 2.9% (Prev. 2.4%)
Swiss CPI MM (Jul) 0.0% vs. Exp. -0.2% (Prev. 0.2%)
Swiss CPI YY (Jul) 0.2% vs. Exp. 0.1% (Prev. 0.1%)
Turkish CPI MM* (Jul) 2.06% vs. Exp. 2.4% (Prev. 1.37%)
Turkish CPI YY* (Jul) 33.52% vs. Exp. 34.05% (Prev. 35.05%)
